Bank evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments for production chat/assistant use in regulated financial services. Key concerns: EU/US data residency, ability to disable/limit logging, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/HIPAA evidence, contract SLAs and pilot benchmarks.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Davis (Prairie State Bank - Head Infra), Samantha Ortiz (CISO), Evan Green (Lead ML Engineer)

Summary: quick discovery on residency and logging. customer very compliance driven, wants private or dedicated options, needs details on logs, encryption, and audit trail retention limits.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan on the account team at Redwood, and with me is Priya from our solutions engineering team. How's everybody doing?
[00:05] Mark Davis: Good, Jordan, thanks. Busy week but excited to chat.
[00:08] Samantha Ortiz: Hi all. I'll be focusing on the compliance bits.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick agenda, we'll ask some background Qs, talk residency options Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, then dig into logging, encryption and contract/SLA needs.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Quick note - I'll jump in on latency and operational stuff, and we can sketch how a POC might look.
[00:25] Evan Green: Sounds good. We have a list of regs – GDPR for our EU customers, PCI-ish restrictions for card data, and HIPAA for a small product line. We also have internal rule that production PII cannot leave the US for some products, and logs need to be scrubbed within 30 days.
[00:40] Jordan Lee: Helpful. On Redwood's side, we support three deployment modes: Hosted (our cloud multi-tenant), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools within regions), and Private (VPC or on-prem bundle). For residency you can pin region or use Private for full customer-controlled network.
[00:55] Samantha Ortiz: When you say Hosted, are logs stored by Redwood? Is there an option to disable request logging?
[01:03] Jordan Lee: By default we retain certain telemetry and request metadata for X days for reliability and fraud detection. But for enterprise customers we have options: we can disable request-level logging, or configure zero-log retention for PII workloads under a dedicated/private contract. I should say though, that the auto-transcription of system logs, sometimes our product names get mumbled in the auto logs, but we offer explicit log redaction and opt-out on a per-route basis.
[01:30] Samantha Ortiz: Do you have SOC 2 and HIPAA attestation? We need a BAA for the healthcare lines.
[01:37] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and a HIPAA/BAA package available for Private and Dedicated customers. For Hosted, we can provide SOC 2 reports and limited HIPAA support depending on contract – but many banks prefer Dedicated or Private for stronger controls.
[01:52] Mark Davis: For data residency: some of our accounts are EU customers and we must ensure EU data never leaves EU. Can you guarantee region pinning at the customer or even route level?
[02:00] Priya Nair: Yes, region pinning is supported. We can route requests to specific regions and enforce that derivatives and cache aren't replicated outside the region. For Private deployments that's customer-managed, so it's fully contained. One caveat: if you want low-latency failover across regions we can do it but that is an opt-in and part of the SLA discussion.
[02:20] Evan Green: About caches – we use prefix caching and KV cache. Are those logs or data persisted? We can't have KV cache write out to S3 in another region.
[02:30] Priya Nair: Good question. The KV cache is in-memory on the serving nodes by default. For Dedicated we can configure persistent caches but they'll be in-region storage. For Hosted, ephemeral caches may be logged to help with cold-starts; we have controls to disable persistent caching and to prevent cross-region replication.
[02:47] Samantha Ortiz: Encryption – do you integrate with our KMS/HSM? Keys must be customer-managed for certain products.
[02:54] Jordan Lee: We support customer-managed keys via KMS in Dedicated and Private, and HSM integrations for Private. Hosted supports server-side encryption with Redwood-managed keys, but we can do CMKs for enterprise contracts. We'll include the key management options in the pack.
[03:10] Mark Davis: Logging retention – our security policy says logs that contain PII must be scrubbed within 30 days and access should be audited. Can you do that?
[03:18] Priya Nair: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can set retention windows, provide audit logs and RBAC. For Hosted we have standard retention policies but can negotiate shorter windows on an enterprise plan and suppress request bodies. We also offer redaction rules and configurable PII scrubbing.
[03:36] Evan Green: Are audit logs immutable? We need tamper-evidence for internal audits.
[03:40] Jordan Lee: We provide append-only audit logs and can integrate with your SIEM and support ingest into your log archive. For Private we can ship directly to your S3 or on-prem archive with retention controls.
[03:52] Samantha Ortiz: What about data subject requests under GDPR? If a EU user requests deletion, can you delete model inputs/derivatives?
[03:58] Priya Nair: We support deletion APIs and can tie into workflows. For Hosted it's supported but you need to coordinate with retention windows; for Dedicated/Private you have more control and faster deletion SLAs. We'll share the DSR process in the docs.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: On the security docs we'll include a mapping for GDPR, PCI-ish, HIPAA clauses and our evidence artifacts.
[04:18] Mark Davis: Our procurement will want explicit wording around data residency and logging in the contract. Can Redwood commit to not using customer prompts for model improvements?
[04:26] Jordan Lee: We do not use customer-provided data to train our public models. For Hosted customers, by default telemetry is used for safety improvements but we offer an opt-out and for Dedicated/Private it's customer-owned. We'll provide contractual language.
[04:38] Evan Green: Performance wise, if we go Dedicated in us-east-1, what's expected latency for 2k tokens?
[04:44] Priya Nair: Typical p95 for steady-state with batching for a model like Redwood-XL at 2k is around 200-400ms for token generation depending on concurrency. We'll propose benchmark tests during POC. Note: transcription sometimes says 'Redwood X L' in our logs, but that's just the speech model, ignore that.
[05:05] Samantha Ortiz: Can we run an on-prem pilot in our lab? We have an air-gapped environment requirement for one product line.
[05:11] Jordan Lee: Yes, our Private on-prem package supports air-gapped installs. It requires lead time for provisioning and entitlements – typical timeline is 6-8 weeks plus compliance scoping.
[05:22] Mark Davis: Ok timeline-wise procurement is Q3, want pilot in July.
[05:25] Jordan Lee: Sounds doable. Proposed next steps: I'll send SOC2/HIPAA docs, network/topology guide, and CMK/HSM options. Priya will schedule the tech deep dive and a benchmark run with Evan. Mark to send list of required controls and target timeline.
[05:40] Evan Green: Also want a short checklist for what evidence you can produce for audits – e.g., encryption key rotation logs, access history.
[05:45] Priya Nair: We'll include an evidence matrix in the package.
[05:48] Jordan Lee: Any other questions?
[05:50] Samantha Ortiz: Not right now. We'll review materials and prioritize pilot scope.
[05:55] Jordan Lee: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and schedule.

Closing notes: call ended ~15:42 UTC. Action items and next steps as listed.

References / shared artifacts: "SOC2-REDWOOD-2025.pdf" (sent post-call), "HIPAA-BAA-template.docx", "redwood-network-topology.pdf", "dedicated-deployment-guide.md".

"Transcription notes": occasional mis-attribution and typical auto-transcribe artifacts; product names may be spelled oddly (e.g., Redwood Dedicated -> "Redwood dedicates").
